BiblicalUsage: Bildad means confusing love, and he is the second of Job's three friends. Job 2:11 brings him with Eliphaz and Zophar when they hear of Job's trouble, and then he speaks three times — Job 8:1, Job 18:1, and Job 25:1 — each speech shorter and harder than the last, until he has nothing left but God's dominion and the smallness of man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bildad shows me how a friend can be right about God's greatness and wrong about his suffering friend, both at once.
